sub_scenario.one_line: hospital bed-flow coordinator: likely to go badly before confirmations arrive

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the unknowns list and closing stale entries.
The bed board review wrapped early today.
Verbal commitments in the afternoon, after confirmations, are painless.
So it is timing, not format.
Someone new shadowed me in the flow office this morning.
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the discharge confirmations into one message before lunch.
During the winter surge I listed which wards' discharges were confirmed versus assumed before committing beds, and we placed forty patients without a single collision.
It is the only tool that matters at scale.
In a true emergency I will commit on partial data and live with it; that is the job.
I archived last cycle's notes on the bed board and set up the new folder.
As fresh as these things get.
Confirmations flow in between 08:40 and 09:10; the proposed huddle change moves commitments to 08:30.
Ten minutes ahead of the data, structurally.
A vendor call about the unknowns list ran long but ended well.
I walked through the flow office checklist with the new starter.
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the discharge confirmations.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the bed board records and fixed it at the source.
At rounds in January I was pressed to commit beds verbally before discharge confirmations came back, and I double-booked the isolation room on an assumption.
It felt confirmed. It was not.
I sketched next week's plan for the discharge confirmations before leaving.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the unknowns list updates.
My night-shift recovery is still shaky and early mornings are when I most need external checklists.
Another layer on the same hours.
I compared two options for the bed board tooling and noted a mild preference.
I closed the week by updating the flow office handover notes.
If the morning huddle switches next week to on-the-spot bed commitments at 08:30, what is the most realistic picture of how my first crunch morning goes?
